title: Show the project URL from the CLI
lead: Someone who has slicer installed can't find out from the command where it came from, where its docs are, or where to report a bug. The help and version output never name the repository.
findings_note: owner request 2026-10-01: repo URL (https://github.com/squalor-xyz/slicer) reachable from -h or --about; today only pyproject.toml has it
boundary: **Not in this slice:** changing --version output; an about subcommand; reading package metadata at runtime; update or new-release checks against the repository.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Owner request (2026-10-01): make the repository URL, https://github.com/squalor-xyz/slicer, reachable from `-h` or an about flag.

Today:
- `--version` prints only `slicer 1.1.0` (`cli.py:1639`).
- `-h` lists the commands under the header "Command line entry point." That is the first line of `cli.py`'s own module docstring (`cli.py:1635`, `description=__doc__.splitlines()[0]`), not a description of slicer.
- The URLs exist only in `pyproject.toml:26-28` (Homepage, Source, Issues). After a PyPI or `pipx` install, the user has no copy of that file.

An agent or user who hits a bug has nowhere to send it without searching the web.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/__init__.py` (a single home for the URL, beside `__version__`)
- `src/slicer/cli.py` (top-level `--about` flag; an epilog and a proper description on the top-level parser)
- `tests/test_cli.py` (output), `tests/test_packaging.py` (URL agrees with `pyproject.toml`)
- `tests/test_docs_coverage.py` only if it enumerates top-level flags
- `README.md` (one line near install or the command table), `docs/commands.md`
- `CHANGELOG.md`

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `-h` output ends with an epilog naming `https://github.com/squalor-xyz/slicer` and the issues URL.
2. `-h` output's description is slicer's one-line description, not "Command line entry point."
3. `--about` prints the name and version, the one-line description, the repository URL and the issues URL, and exits 0. It needs no project: it works in an empty directory, the way `--version` does.
4. `--about --json` prints `{"name", "version", "description", "url", "issues"}` and exits 0.
5. `--version` output is unchanged (`slicer X.Y.Z`), because scripts may parse it.
6. A packaging test asserts that the URL constant equals `[project.urls].Source` in `pyproject.toml`, and the issues URL equals `Issues`, so the two can't drift. This mirrors the existing single-home `__version__` test (`test_packaging.py:38-44`).

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Add `__url__ = "https://github.com/squalor-xyz/slicer"` to `src/slicer/__init__.py`, and derive the issues URL from it (`__url__ + "/issues"`). Do not read `importlib.metadata`: the suite and CI run uninstalled from `src/` (AGENTS.md), where package metadata is absent.

On the top-level parser in `build_parser`:
- set `description` to the package docstring's first line, "roadmap and slice manager", rather than `cli.py`'s own docstring;
- add an `epilog` with the project and issues URLs.

Register `--about` as a top-level flag. It acts the way `--version` does: print, then exit before the subcommand is required. Since that has to honour `--json`, the cleanest route is to handle `--about` in `main` before the subcommand is required, rather than as an argparse action. Pick whichever keeps `--about` working without a subcommand and keeps the exit code at 0.

Add one README line ("Source and issues: …", or note that `--about` prints them) and a `docs/commands.md` mention.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: The failing tests pass, then `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests`, `slicer check` and `git diff --check`.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch, including the re-rendered roadmap and a CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased.
